svg.title: Margin-configurable two-path delay network: 70-tap example
svg.desc: A uniform 70-tap passive accumulator is factored as H2(D) times H5(D squared) times H7(D to the tenth). Each Hn is the normalized sum of n consecutive delays. The 5-tap group uses a direct path and a delayed 4-tap path with matched splitter and combiner power ratios one fifth and four fifths. The 7-tap group similarly uses a direct path and a delayed 6-tap path with ratios one seventh and six sevenths. Its 6-tap branch contains a balanced 2-tap cell and a nested 3-tap two-arm network, whose ratios are one third and two thirds. No junction splits into three paths. There are eight cells: five balanced and three unequal joins. The network creates a 390-picosecond completed plateau for a 320-picosecond input frame, leaving 35 picoseconds of margin on either side of the centered useful window. Frames alternate between two networks every 400 picoseconds. No output shutter is used. Receiving nonlinear conversion, replay and memory capture must respect valid windows. The final panel defines how to choose the tap count from a requested fractional plateau increase and absolute left and right arrival budgets. Device settling, phase and bandwidth performance remain unvalidated.

g.text: Margin-configurable delay network · two-way junctions only
Example: R = 32 terms · τ = 10 ps · L = 70 taps · 390 ps plateau for a 320 ps useful input · no output shutter
ONE PASSIVE ACCUMULATOR · nested branch filters produce exactly 70 uniform taps
Hₙ(z) = (1 + z + ⋯ + zⁿ⁻¹) / n. Blocks multiply in sequence; weighted joins add their two branch fields.
H₇₀(D) = H₂(D) H₅(D²) H₇(D¹⁰) = (1 + D + ⋯ + D⁶⁹) / 70
8 cells = 5 balanced + 3 unequal joins. Both couplers of each join use the stated power ratios; branch phases are calibrated.
DUAL-NETWORK READ SCHEDULE · 390 ps completed plateau, with a centered 320 ps acceptance window
35 ps per edge is an engineered arrival / settling budget, not a validated tolerance. Receiver pump edges must satisfy their own waveform model.
Frames alternate every 400 ps; each network is revisited every 800 ps. Ideal reader-core duty = 80%; separate writes still need time.
Delay sum = 69τ = 690 ps; differential path = 103.5 mm per network, 207 mm per pair at n_g = 2. Largest single delay = 200 ps.
OUTPUT SELECTOR CHANGEOVER · the receiver rejects light during this 80 ps interval
No output darkness is assumed. Next DFG: timed coefficient pump accepts useful light; its B filter rejects the unconverted input.
The 50 ps selector transition is not a pump-edge allowance. A wider input plateau does not make unintended converted tails valid terms.
COMPARISON · the 70-tap example supplies 21.875% more plateau duration than the 320 ps useful frame
DESIGN THE MARGINS · choose a plateau requirement first, then synthesize the two-path network
T_required = max[(1 + μ) T_in, T_in + g_left + g_right] L = R − 1 + ceil(T_required / τ)
For μ = 20% total and T_in = 320 ps: T_required = 384 ps → L = 70 → T_valid = 390 ps → 35 ps per edge if centered.
Specify g_left and g_right from arrival uncertainty, settling and other waveform requirements; use asymmetric placement when needed.
Any integer L can use nested two-arm joins; ordinary balanced doubling alone rounds to powers of two. Check frame-reuse interference too.
All lengths omit common routing. Physical coupler bandwidth, branch loss, phase stability and receiver waveform requirements remain to be validated.
